turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the device stack

**What the training set says about high‑efficiency n–i–p MAPbI₃ stacks:**

1. **Best ETLs are compact metal oxides with a passivating/cascade overlayer.** The very top entries all use a bilayer where a fullerene or a wide‑gap oxide nanoparticle layer sits on TiO₂‑c: `TiO2-c | SnO2-np` + Spiro (20.85), `TiO2-c | PCBM-60` (19.35, 17.2 with C60, 16.4), `TiO2-c | BaSnO3-np` + PTAA (18.9), `SnO2-c | PCBM-60` (17.3–18.0), `ZnO-np | PCBM-60` (18.1). Physically: the TiO₂ gives a continuous hole‑blocking contact, while the fullerene/SnO₂ overlayer passivates surface Ti³⁺/oxygen‑vacancy traps, removes the electron extraction barrier and suppresses interfacial recombination and hysteresis → high V_OC and FF.
2. **Best HTLs are doped Spiro‑OMeTAD, PTAA, or a well‑matched conjugated polymer (PCDTBT family)**, and an **interlayer between perovskite and HTL** (PMMA|Spiro 18.0, PbS‑QDs|Spiro 18.6, IEICO‑4F|Spiro 19.0, GO|Spiro 16.2) consistently adds 1–2 % absolute by passivating the perovskite surface while keeping hole transfer fast.
3. **Fully evaporated doped‑organic stacks (TaTm / F6‑TCNNQ with C60:PhIm)** reach 17.9 in the training set — pinhole‑free, perfectly selective ohmic contacts.
4. **Penalties:** carbon/HTL‑free stacks, flexible PEN/PET substrates, mesoporous‑only ZnO or CdS/oxide ETLs without passivation, P3HT (undoped, shallow HOMO → V_OC loss), and metal phthalocyanine/small‑molecule HTLs.

**Applying this to the pool:**

- **c064** `TiO2-c | SnO2-np / Spiro / Au` — the exact motif of the 20.85 % champion recipe (only Au instead of Ag); ideal conduction‑band cascade FTO→TiO₂→SnO₂ with trap‑passivated SnO₂ surface. Highest expected.
- **c005** `TiO2-c | PCBM-60 / PCDTBT8 / MoO3|Au` — direct analogue of the 19.35 % PCDTBT1 device; fullerene‑passivated TiO₂ plus a deep‑HOMO polymer HTL with MoO₃ hole‑injection buffer.
- **c017** `C60;PhIm | C60 / TaTm|F6-TCNNQ:TaTm / Ag`, co‑evaporated — twin of the 17.9 % all‑evaporated p‑i‑n‑selective stack; doped transport layers give ohmic contacts and negligible series resistance.
- **c043** `TiO2-c | TiO2-mp / DAHI | Spiro / Au` — mesoporous TiO₂ with an added organic passivation interlayer between absorber and Spiro, the same lever that gave 18.0 (PMMA|Spiro) and 17.4 (aminocaproic acid).
- **c080** `TiO2-c | MPMIC60 / Spiro / Ag` — fullerene‑derivative‑modified TiO₂ (trap passivation, hysteresis suppression) with doped Spiro; matches the 17.2–17.5 % class.

(Close runners‑up: c073 TiO₂‑c|C60/PTAA, c021 SnO₂‑np|CPTA, c045 TiO₂‑nanofibres/PTAA, c078 Al₂O₃|NiO/Spiro.)

**Final: c064, c005, c017, c043, c080**
